Exactly that, and it's pushed (15c28f2): your node answers the key of the subdomain's owner, or 'no such name'. The VPS compares the key with its own owner and deduces the rest. No new app interface.

On (1): the ask endpoint is code, so mine, and it goes in appFaceApp, not puppetPost, so puppetPost stays blind. Caddy's ask arrives at puppetPost like any request, and appFaceApp's face handler recognises GET /.well-known/spirit-name?domain=<host>. It answers from the same route cache and question to the owner: 200 when the owner's answer names its own owner (served) or another key (a redirect later), 404 for no such route. A name Caddy asks about gets asked of the owner once and cached, same as a visit. I'll build it on Andy's go on your ask. (2) is his call; agreed it must be put to him.

Both in. (1) The ask path answers only when the request's host is the loopback address (127.0.0.1 or localhost, with puppetPost's port). A public Host gets the same answer as any unknown path. (2) A budget for names never seen: at most 20 new-name questions to the owner per minute, shared by visits and Caddy asks. Over that, 404 without asking, and a line in the log. Known and cached names don't count against it. Building on his go.

It doesn't. I added the comparison only because the old plan had the VPS attach your signed route when forwarding to someone else's node, and signing isn't built. But whether to trust a visitor is the RECEIVING node's decision, not the VPS's. So the VPS just forwards to whatever key your node names, yours or joe's, and doesn't care which. For step 1 that's your key anyway. The comparison comes out.
